partes.p: (5) Still using the values of $a$ and $b$ from part (a), compute $\displaystyle\int_{C} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$ along the curve $C$ such that $x = e^{t}\cos t$, $y = e^{t}\sin t$, $0 \leq t \leq \pi$.
(10) For $\vec{F} = yx^{3}\,\hat{\imath} + y^{2}\,\hat{\jmath}$, find $\displaystyle\int_{C} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}$ on the portion of the curve $y = x^{2}$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(1, 1)$.
(5) Let $C$ be a simple closed curve going counterclockwise around a region $R$. Let $M = M(x, y)$. Express $\displaystyle\oint_{C} M\,dx$ as a double integral over $R$.
(5) Find $M$ so that $\displaystyle\oint_{C} M\,dx$ is the mass of $R$ with density $\delta(x, y) = (x + y)^{2}$.
